subject: Competitive Playbook: recap + agreed validation tests
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vargas <elena@stitchdata.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@finex.co>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Competitive Playbook: recap + agreed validation tests

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick write-up from our discovery so we have aligned expectations before the hands-on validation:

Key pain points you emphasized
- Inconsistent latency under burst traffic for real-time orchestration (p95 spikes up to ~850ms at peak)
- Cost unpredictability as models scale across geographies (token spend + egress)
- Lack of straightforward fallbacks when a model variant hits capacity (current solution requires manual re-routing)

Customer goals we heard
- Stable p95 < 250ms for interactive flows (US-east), with predictable autoscale behavior
- 30–40% reduction in token unit cost for high-throughput batch tasks
- Built-in fallback routing and audit logs for compliance checks

Competitive context
- You're running a mix of self-hosted endpoints and a managed provider; asked us to show where Redwood would materially improve latency & cost while supporting private VPC controls.

Agreed validation tests (what we will run together)
1) Latency stress profile — live ramp in US-east with synthetic traffic to measure p50/p95, CPU/GPU utilization, and cold-starts
2) Cost projection test — small 48-hour run vs recorded production trace to estimate unit economics and expected monthly spend at current QPS
3) Fallback scenario — force model variant A into simulated capacity exhaustion and validate automatic routing to variant B and audit trail creation
4) Quality sanity check — 50 seeded prompts from your evaluation set to ensure no regression from quantized variants

Attachments: I attached a short validation checklist and a one-pager comparing our runtime behaviors to a typical peer (stitch-validation-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-vs-peer-brief.pdf).

Next steps / asks
- Can you confirm the target window for the validation (you mentioned next Tue/Wed in the call)?
- Please share a short sample of the production trace (anonymized) for the cost projection run — S3 link or zip is fine.
- Who on your infra team should we coordinate with for VPC/network setup (ticket and IAM)?

I’ll loop in Neha to draft a compact mutual action plan and a live-test agenda. If those goals look off, tell me and I’ll update the plan.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Competitive Playbook: recap + agreed validation tests

Vivek,

Appreciate the recap — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple clarifications:
- The target validation window: Wed 2026-12-09 10:00–14:00 ET (we have a maintenance window afterwards).
- Production trace: I’ll upload an anonymized 24-hour trace to the S3 share and send the link by EOD.
- Infra contact: Tom Hsu (cc’d) will be the point for VPC peering and IAM — he prefers Slack for quick coordination.

One additional ask: can Redwood run the fallback scenario using our current routing policy so we can compare the manual steps we take today vs automatic routing? That will be the most convincing part for our architecture review board.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Engineering, StitchData

1) Validation window confirmed: Wed 12/09 10:00–14:00 ET. We need to have infra handshake complete by Tue EOD (12/08) or we risk losing the maintenance window.
2) Test owners: Sean to own latency stress profile + fallback automation test. Vivek to own cost projection run and customer-facing QA. I’ll coordinate the logistics and create the runbook.
3) Infra tasks for Tom Hsu:
   - VPC peering + security group allow list (we need his public CIDR for the test harness)

4) Risk notes:

Action items:
- Sean: draft the short stress script and smoke test by Tue 12/08 12:00pm ET. Attach to runbook.
- Vivek: finalize email to Elena confirming the window and request the S3 link (I can take the doc for the runbook after you send).
